newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks fall sharply on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks fall sharply on profit-taking.

text.p: Caracas stocks fell sharply on a wave of profit-taking, closing down 2.64 percent, traders said.
The market's leading 19-share .IBC index finished 177.883 points down, to close at 6,559.06, indicating that a recent three-week rally might be over.
"This is a rather healthy reaction and will allow (investors) to take positions again," Roberto Isasi, of Merinvest brokerage said.
He said some of the investors who went in last month are beginning to pull out and that triggered a chain reaction.

Among traded issues, 34 fell, eight rose and two closed flat. With only 28.65 million shares traded, according to preliminary figures, the market was relatively quiet. Trading was worth 3.84 billion bolivars ($8.06 million).
Some traders said Venezuela's troubled social situation, with a lingering public doctors' strike, could also explain the bolsa's drop.
"What happens on the social front undoubtedly affects capital markets," Vencred broker Geronimo Paolini said.
Public doctors voted Thursday to suspend their strike for a week and agreed to resume work at emergency services but maintained their demand for a big pay increase.
